scope: Proposition 3.4 of the manuscript “A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-Naimarks-problem-in-ZFC-September-24-2026/naimark-counterexample-zfc.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 297 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5f8f878435bb9440), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let O be a unital faithfully tracial C∗-algebra. For each t ∈ {j, k}, let Dt 1, Dt 2 ⊂ O, Et i : O → Dt i and θt : Dt 1 → Dt 2 satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition 3.1. When forming an adjunction over Hj(O) or Hk(O), extend the other data expectations by composition with the expectation onto O. There is a trace-preserving isomorphism Hk(Hj(O)) ∼ = Hj(Hk(O)) (3.8) fixing O and the named stable unitaries vj, vk.
